Key Takeaways
  • Nepali students can apply directly to UK undergraduate programs after completing +2 (NEB or equivalent) with a minimum of 50–60% marks.
  • Most universities require an IELTS Academic score of 6.0–6.5 overall, with no band below 5.5.
  • UK student visa (Student Route) requires a CAS letter, proof of funds, and a valid IELTS/TOEFL score.
  • Annual tuition for international students ranges from GBP 12,000 to GBP 25,000 — living costs add GBP 900–1,400 per month.
  • The Chevening Scholarship and Commonwealth Scholarships offer fully funded opportunities, primarily for postgraduate study.
  • After graduation, a 2-year Graduate Route visa allows students to work freely in the UK without a job offer.

Every year, a growing number of Nepali students choose the United Kingdom as their study destination — and it is easy to understand why. The UK is home to universities such as Oxford, Cambridge, UCL, the University of Edinburgh, and over 160 other globally recognized institutions. A British degree is respected by employers worldwide and, in many fields, opens doors that simply would not be accessible otherwise.

However, studying in the UK is also one of the more complex and expensive options for Nepali students. As a result, it requires careful planning, early preparation, and a thorough understanding of the requirements. In this complete guide, we walk you through every step of the process — so that you can make an informed, confident decision about your future.

Why Nepali Students Choose the United Kingdom

The United Kingdom offers several compelling advantages for international students that go beyond the prestige of its university names. To begin with, UK undergraduate programs are typically three years in duration — one year shorter than equivalent programs in Nepal, Australia, or the United States. This not only saves money but gets you into the workforce faster.

Furthermore, the UK's Graduate Route visa — introduced in 2021 — allows international students to remain in the UK for two years after graduation (three years for PhD graduates) to work, look for jobs, or start a business. This pathway has made the UK a far more attractive destination than it was even five years ago.

Additionally, the UK's multicultural environment, world-class research infrastructure, and strong industry connections — particularly in finance, law, engineering, and creative industries — make it an excellent choice for students with ambitious career goals.

Can You Study in the UK After +2? What Universities Require

The short answer is yes — Nepali students who have completed their +2 from NEB (National Examinations Board) or an equivalent A-Level program are eligible to apply for undergraduate programs at UK universities. Here is what you will need to demonstrate for a standard UK undergraduate application:

📋
Academic Qualification
Completed +2 from NEB or equivalent. Most universities accept NEB results directly.
Min. 50–65% in +2
🗣️
English Proficiency
IELTS Academic is most widely accepted. TOEFL iBT and PTE Academic also accepted.
IELTS 6.0–6.5 overall
📝
Personal Statement
A well-written statement via UCAS explaining your motivation, goals, and relevant experience.
4,000 characters max
📌
Reference Letter
One academic reference from a teacher or school principal submitted through UCAS.
1 academic reference
🏛️
UCAS Application
All UK undergraduate applications are processed through UCAS. Apply to up to 5 universities at once.
Up to 5 choices
💰
Financial Evidence
Proof that you can cover tuition and living costs for at least the first year of your studies.
GBP 30,000–45,000+
Important Note for NEB Students: Some highly competitive UK universities — particularly Russell Group institutions like UCL, King's College London, and the University of Edinburgh — may require higher academic grades and subject-specific prerequisites. Always check individual course requirements on the university website.

IELTS Requirements for UK Study from Nepal

English proficiency is one of the most critical requirements for studying in the UK. The vast majority of UK universities accept IELTS Academic as their primary evidence of English proficiency. Below are the typical IELTS score ranges you should aim for, depending on where you plan to apply:

6.0
Standard entry for most foundation and pre-degree programs
6.5
Most mid-ranked UK universities for undergraduate programs
7.0
Top universities: UCL, Edinburgh, LSE, King's College
7.5
Oxford, Cambridge, and highly competitive programs
5.5 min
Minimum per band for most universities at overall 6.0
6.0 min
Minimum per band for institutions requiring 6.5 overall

Importantly, achieving the overall band score is not enough — most universities also impose minimum band requirements for individual sections (listening, reading, writing, speaking). In Nepal, IELTS tests are conducted by the British Council and IDP Education in Kathmandu and other major cities. The test costs approximately NPR 25,000–28,000 and results are typically available within 13 days for the paper-based test, or 3–5 days for the computer-delivered test.

How Much Does It Cost to Study in the UK from Nepal?

It would be dishonest to say that studying in the UK is cheap — it is not. The UK is one of the more expensive study destinations for Nepali students. However, understanding the full cost picture helps you plan effectively, and there are several ways to manage expenses through scholarships, part-time work, and choosing the right city.

Expense Details Estimated Annual Cost
Tuition Fees Varies by university and course GBP 12,000–25,000
Accommodation University halls or private rental GBP 6,000–12,000
Food & Groceries Self-catering, cooking at home GBP 2,400–3,600
Transport Student railcard and local transport GBP 600–1,500
Books & Supplies Library access reduces cost GBP 500–1,000
Health Surcharge (IHS) Paid with visa application (per year) GBP 776/year
Personal & Leisure Travel, social activities GBP 1,200–2,400
Total Estimated (Outside London) Based on mid-range estimates GBP 24,000–38,000/year

Students who choose universities in cities such as Sheffield, Manchester, Leeds, Edinburgh, or Birmingham can often reduce their living costs by 20–30% compared to London. UK Student Visa holders can work up to 20 hours per week during term time, contributing GBP 5,000–8,000 per year toward living expenses.

Scholarships Available for Nepali Students Studying in the UK

🏆
Chevening Scholarship
The UK government's flagship international scholarship program. Fully funded — covers tuition, living costs, flights, and visa fees. Open to outstanding Nepali students for one-year master's programs. Requires two years of work experience and strong leadership potential.
Fully Funded Postgraduate Only Leadership Focus
🌐
Commonwealth Scholarships
Administered by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission, these fully funded awards are available for postgraduate students from commonwealth countries including Nepal. The focus is on development-relevant study that benefits the student's home country upon return.
Fully Funded Postgraduate Only Development Focus
🎓
University-Specific Merit Scholarships
Many UK universities offer international student scholarships ranging from GBP 2,000 to GBP 10,000 per year based on academic excellence. Universities such as the University of Aberdeen and University of Stirling actively award merit scholarships to Nepali students.
Undergraduate Available Postgraduate Available Merit Based
🔬
GREAT Scholarship
A partnership between the British Council and UK universities, the GREAT Scholarship offers GBP 10,000 toward postgraduate tuition for students from eligible countries including Nepal. Available through participating UK universities and is highly competitive.
GBP 10,000 Award Postgraduate Only

UK Student Visa for Nepali Students: Everything You Need to Know

To study in the UK, Nepali students must apply for a UK Student Visa — formally known as the Student Route visa. The most important thing to understand is that you can only apply for this visa after receiving a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from a Home Office-licensed UK university.

Documents Required for UK Student Visa

  • CAS Number — Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies issued by your UK university
  • Valid Passport — must be valid for the duration of your course plus additional time
  • IELTS / TOEFL Score — meeting the minimum requirement of your university
  • Proof of Funds — bank statements showing you can cover tuition + GBP 1,334/month for living (London) or GBP 1,023/month (outside London)
  • Academic Transcripts — +2 mark sheets, certificates, and any prior qualifications
  • Tuberculosis (TB) Test — mandatory for Nepali students applying for UK student visa
  • IHS Payment Receipt — Immigration Health Surcharge of GBP 776 per year paid online
  • Biometric Information — collected at a Visa Application Center in Kathmandu
TB Test Requirement: Nepal is on the UK's list of countries where TB testing is mandatory for visa applicants. You must take an approved TB test at a certified clinic in Nepal (typically at CIWEC or similar approved centers in Kathmandu) before submitting your visa application. Results are valid for six months.

The UK Student Visa application fee is currently GBP 490 (applied from outside the UK). You should apply no earlier than six months before your course starts, and at least three months in advance to allow sufficient processing time. Most applications are processed within three weeks.

Step-by-Step: How to Apply to UK Universities from Nepal

The UK university application process follows a structured timeline. Starting early is absolutely essential — ideally 12 to 18 months before your intended start date.

1
Research Universities and Courses
18 months before intake
Use UCAS, university websites, and tools like The Complete University Guide to compare programs, entry requirements, fees, and rankings. Shortlist 5–7 universities that match your academic profile, budget, and career goals.
2
Prepare and Take IELTS
12–15 months before intake
Register for IELTS Academic through the British Council or IDP in Nepal. Allow at least 2–3 months of dedicated preparation. IELTS scores are valid for two years and most universities accept your best result.
3
Write Your UCAS Personal Statement
12 months before intake
Your personal statement is a 4,000-character essay submitted through UCAS explaining why you want to study your chosen subject, what makes you a strong candidate, and what you hope to achieve. One personal statement is submitted for all five universities.
4
Submit UCAS Application
October–January (year before intake)
The standard UCAS deadline for most undergraduate courses is January 29. For Oxford, Cambridge, and medicine/dentistry programs, the deadline is October 15 — significantly earlier. Apply to up to 5 universities at once.
5
Receive Offers and Reply via UCAS
February–June
Universities will send conditional or unconditional offers through UCAS. Once you receive all decisions, you select one firm choice and one insurance choice through UCAS Track.
6
Apply for Scholarships
Running concurrently
Research and apply for all available scholarships — university-specific awards, Chevening (opens August–November), GREAT Scholarship, and British Council grants. Many scholarships have early deadlines, so this runs parallel to your university application.
7
Receive CAS and Apply for UK Student Visa
3–4 months before course start
Once your place is confirmed, your university will issue a CAS number. Use this to apply for your UK Student Visa online. Book your biometric appointment at the British Embassy VAC in Kathmandu and complete your TB test beforehand.
8
Pre-Departure Preparation and Travel to the UK
4–8 weeks before course start
Once your visa is approved, arrange your accommodation, book flights, open a UK bank account if possible, attend pre-departure orientations, and connect with Nepali student communities at your university.
"A UK degree is not just a qualification — it is a three-year investment in your global career. With the right preparation and support, Nepali students can access some of the world's finest universities and build truly international futures."

Most Popular Courses for Nepali Students in the UK

While Nepali students pursue a wide range of subjects in the UK, certain fields are particularly popular. Business and Management remains the most commonly chosen field, with programs available at virtually every UK university and strong links to London's financial services industry. Computer Science and IT are increasingly popular given the UK's growing tech sector and the global demand for software engineering skills.

Healthcare and Nursing programs have seen a significant increase in Nepali student applications, particularly following the UK's active international nurse recruitment drive. Similarly, Engineering programs — especially civil, mechanical, and electrical engineering — are in high demand due to the UK's world-class research facilities. Additionally, subjects like Architecture, Hospitality and Tourism Management, and Media and Communication consistently attract Nepali students looking for creative, globally applicable qualifications.

What Happens After You Graduate in the UK?

After completing any undergraduate or master's degree from a licensed UK university, you are eligible to apply for the Graduate Route visa, which allows you to stay and work in the UK for two years without needing a job offer or employer sponsorship. PhD graduates receive three years under this route.

During this period, you can work in any job at any level — giving you the flexibility to build UK work experience, explore different industries, or transition to a skilled worker visa if you secure a sponsored position. Moreover, many Nepali graduates who return home find that their UK qualification significantly enhances their career prospects, salary expectations, and entrepreneurial opportunities in Nepal's growing economy.

It also requires a minimum of two years of work or leadership experience. Applications typically open in August and close in November each year.

To summarize, studying in the UK after +2 from Nepal is absolutely achievable — but it demands early planning, strong academic preparation, and careful financial management. The rewards, however, are significant: a globally respected degree, real post-study work rights, and a career trajectory that can take you anywhere in the world.
